cohort: The study included eleven adult participants with a mean age of 56.09 years (range: 27-79) who were diagnosed with malignant neoplasm and undergoing outpatient chemotherapy treatment.
finding: The study found that patients generally had low to moderate cardiovascular risk correlating with age, experienced a reduction in Quality of Life and an increase in perceived symptom severity across 6 chemotherapy sessions, and identified neuropsychological and fatigue-difficulty sleeping as prevalent symptom clusters.
